chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every emancipation is valid for the newborn, except in the case of the blood-guilt expiation, for indeed Allah the Exalted says, "So free a believing slave" (32:18), meaning one who has reached puberty. And in the case of Dhihar, a child born in Islam is sufficient. And in the expiation of the oath, a garment that covers his private parts is sufficient,' and he said, 'Two garments.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions for manumission as an expiation for murder versus Dhihar in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific criteria for 'manumission of a slave' (tahriq raqabah) as expiation (kaffarah), distinguishing between the requirement of maturity (baligh) for murder and the sufficiency of a child or garment for Dhihar and oaths. It highlights the Shia scholarly interpretation that 'raqabah' in the context of murder implies a mature, believing slave, while allowing flexibility for lesser expiations. This distinction underscores the jurisprudential nuance in applying Quranic verses to different categories of sins.
